1.name: Coupling
1.label: Bidirectional Coupling (Loop Closure)
1.description: Is a specific live physical instance in an automated two-way loop with the model?

levels.label: Digital Model
levels.text: no automated flow to a specific physical instance; built and validated offline against static or historical data (precomputed library, offline design model).

levels.label: Digital Shadow
levels.text: automated flow in one direction only, or the loop is closed for a non-scientific subsystem (e.g. robot motion) while the chemistry stays open.

levels.label: Digital Twin
levels.text: automated bidirectional flow, in which measurements update the model and model predictions steer the next physical action, continuously, on one live instance.

2.name: Fidelity
2.label: Forward-Model Fidelity
2.description: What is the forward map made of?

levels.label: Surrogate
levels.text: fast data-driven or statistical approximator (discrete-event simulation, pure ML or GP emulator); no explicit first-principles physics in the forward map.

levels.label: Hybrid
levels.text: reduced-physics or coarse-grained model with learned components, or a physics engine with approximate kinetics.

levels.label: Faithful mirror
levels.text: first-principles or ab initio forward calculation (DFT, resolved electrochemical–thermal PDEs, mechanistic CRN) meant to reproduce the physics and not just the observable.

3.name: Cost side
3.label: Cost Side
3.description: Once the twin exists, which side, digital or physical, is the bottleneck per iteration (or per use, R6)?

levels.text: digital side dominates; each evaluation is an expensive simulation, and the physical measurement is cheap or absent.
digital-leaning.
both comparable and non-trivial.
physical-leaning.
physical side dominates (scarce beamtime, robotic synthesis, real QPU time); model evaluation is cheap by comparison.

3.guidance: Score by reported wall-clock time or cost per iteration. Only the running cost is scored; one-time costs of building the twin (simulation libraries, model training, calibration data) are not.

4.name: Model dimensionality
4.label: Model Dimensionality (log₁₀ N)
4.note: log10 of parameters fitted to data from the system's own campaign (measured or computed)
4.description: N is the number of model parameters fitted or fine-tuned to data from the system's own campaign, measured or computed (R7). N = 0 scores 0. Pretrained weights, parameters fitted to literature or community data, hand-set constants, and first-principles quantities are excluded.

levels.text: N ≤ 10 (rate constants, bond energies); identifiable from one campaign.
10 < N ≤ 10³ (physics model with calibrated parameters, small neural terms).
10³ < N ≤ 10⁶ (neural surrogates, deep-kernel feature extractors trained on own data).
N > 10⁶ (large networks fine-tuned on own data; not identifiable from a single campaign).

4.guidance: Count parameters from the architecture when the paper or its code gives one, and show the arithmetic in the rationale.

5.name: VVUQ
5.label: VVUQ Maturity
5.description: How strong is the evidence that the model's predictions can be trusted? Levels climb from no comparison with data to a documented credibility assessment.

levels.label: None
levels.text: no comparison with independent data; no uncertainty quantified.

levels.label: Point agreement
levels.text: outputs compared with data (overlays, parity, success rates, benchmark values), with no held-out split and no UQ.

levels.label: Validation or UQ
levels.text: either validation against data not used to build or fit the model, or quantified predictive uncertainty (GP posterior, ensemble variance, functional bracketing).

levels.label: Validation and UQ
levels.text: both, with uncertainty propagated from inputs or measurements to predictions, or checked against data (calibration or coverage tests).

levels.label: Credibility
levels.text: a structured credibility assessment for a stated context of use (e.g. ASME V&V 40), or an error budget covering measurement, data, modeling, and interpretation errors.

6.name: Autonomy
6.label: Autonomy
6.description: How much of the decide–act–update cycle runs without a person? This is scored separately from automation of data flow (Axis 1).

levels.label: Human-in-loop
levels.text: a human picks the next step and interprets results.

levels.label: Semi-autonomous
levels.text: the system decides some steps (e.g. acquisition picks the next sample) with human oversight.

levels.label: Autonomous or agentic
levels.text: runs the decide–act–update cycle over many iterations with essentially no human intervention.
